messages:
tara: quick heads-up — just brought omega-v2 (canary, int8-q5 build) into the onboarding harness against the 'passport' locale set. seeing weird numeral splits in zh/ja sequences (e.g. passport numbers and dates) :thinking:
hiro: can you paste an example tokenization?
tara: sure — example input:
```
护照号码：G12345678
出生日期：1990年01月02日
```

tara: what we expect after detok: `护照号码：G12345678` and `出生日期：1990年01月02日`
sam: what did the tokenizer produce?
tara: tokenized (space for clarity): `护 照 号 码 ： G 123 456 78` — it split the numeric into 3 subtokens instead of preserving `G12345678`. same for dates: `1990 年 01 月 02 日` turned into `199 0 年 01 ...` (weird mid-num split).
ji-won: that smells like a sentencepiece merge rule interacting badly with quantized kernel alignment or kvcache boundary. did we swap tokenizers in the build?
tara: build uses our internal sentencepiece v0.1.96 + legacy normalizer. earlier cpu-onboard (float32) didn't show the split. float32 baseline preserved G+digits as one token. only int8 q5 variant shows it.
eval-bot: quick metrics from the canary run:
- BLEU on passport-test: baseline float32 92.1 -> canary int8-q5 86.3 (delta -5.8)
- chrF: 0.872 -> 0.821
- Tokenization mismatch rate (exact string compare detok): 0.004 -> 0.037
(reported at 2026-03-21T12:34:10Z)
hiro: that's a significant tokenization-induced quality regression. could be a dropped normalization step or an encoding/byte-level difference produced by the quant runtime path.
olivia: any differences in pretokenizer config? we recently enabled `enable_nbsp_preserve=true` on some builds. could that affect numeric merges?
tara: good call — i compared config files: float32 had `use_legacy_digit_grouping=false` while canary int8 had it true (weird). i didn't change that intentionally.
sam: who touched tokenizer config in the onboarding pipeline?
ji-won: i deployed a change two days ago to make pretokenizer fallback faster on GPU; it toggles digit grouping when encountering alnum runs to avoid oversized tokens. maybe it slipped into the canary image.
tara: reproduction steps i used:
1) checkout `onboard/canary/omega-v2-int8-q5`
2) run `./tools/run_tokenizer_check --file passport-test.jsonl --mode detok`
3) inspect badcases: `jq '.badcases[] | {input,detok_expected,detok_observed}' out.json`

sam: quick experiment idea — rerun tokenizer with the exact float32 tokenizer binary against the int8 model path to see if the model or the tokenizer binary is at fault. if detok still matches float baseline, it's model.
tara: did that — projection: when running float32 tokenizer binary + int8 model, detok preserved G12345678. when running int8 tokenizer binary + float32 model, splits happened. so tokenizer branch is the culprit.
ji-won: ok that narrows it. i'm going to bisect the tokenizer commits in `onboard/tokenizers` between v1.14.2 and HEAD. will report back.
eval-bot: added failing example `6571234567-1` to the eval dashboard and flagged regression alert (quality-regressions:medium).
hiro: potential quick mitigation — add a temporary patch to force `digit_grouping=legacy=false` in onboarding config for canary images until we identify root cause. also add a smoke test asserting passport numeric preservation.
tara: agreed. i'll open a patch and PR the smoke test.
olivia: assign me review — also can we add a small unit test for date formats across ja/zh/ko locales? want to avoid collateral breaks.
sam: noted. once ji-won finishes the bisect, let's decide whether to rollback the tokenizer change or tweak the pretokenizer heuristics. :eyes:
ji-won: bisect in progress — hitting one commit that modified `alnum-run` splitter. suspicion rising. will ping when i have the exact commit id.
tara: thanks team. keeping this in canary until we roll out mitigations. will update thread with PR link. :thumbsup:
olivia: nice triage, good signal-to-noise on the passport set — this is exactly why we run localized smoke.
(olivia reacted :thumbsup: to tara's message)
